identification.summary: Educated Manticore is Check Point Research's name for an Iranian-aligned activity cluster first publicly reported in April 2023, which Check Point said overlaps strongly with Phosphorus (Microsoft: Mint Sandstorm) [S2]. It used the PowerLess backdoor delivered through ISO images with Iraq-themed decoys in Arabic, English and Hebrew [S2]. In June 2025 Check Point reported the cluster running spear-phishing against Israeli journalists, cybersecurity experts and computer science professors [S4][S5].
identification.firstObserved: Publicly reported by Check Point Research in 2023-04 [S2]. Earlier activity date not stated in the sources gathered.
identification.notes: Check Point tracks this as a cluster, not a named state unit. In 2023 it said it lacked sufficient knowledge to place PowerLess activity within the wider Iranian landscape and so gave it its own name [S2]. In 2025 Check Point said the cluster aligns with activity the wider community tracks as APT42, Charming Kitten or Mint Sandstorm [S5]. Other vendor names for the broader Phosphorus family cited in coverage: APT35, TA453, Cobalt Illusion, ITG18, Yellow Garuda [S2]. Do not merge facts from those clusters into this record without cluster-specific sourcing.

attribution.sponsor: Iran. Check Point says the cluster is believed to work for the IRGC Intelligence Organization (IRGC-IO) [S5].
attribution.confidence: Check Point (2023) described strong overlap with Phosphorus/Mint Sandstorm but declined to fully attribute the activity [S2]. Check Point (2025) stated the IRGC-IO assessment as a belief [S5]. No government attribution found in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Check Point tooling and infrastructure analysis (PowerLess backdoor, ISO lures, phishing kits) as relayed in secondary coverage; I could not open the Check Point reports directly [S2][S4][S5].

objectives: Espionage and credential theft against Israel-linked individuals and the research community, including academics and cybersecurity experts [S2][S4][S5]. Specific collection requirements are not stated in the sources gathered.

sectors: Technology sector (executives and researchers impersonated as lures)
targeting.notes: 2023: decoy content from the Arab Science and Technology Foundation led Check Point to conclude the research community may have been targeted [S2]. 2025: victims included Israeli journalists, high-profile cybersecurity experts and computer science professors from leading Israeli universities; Check Point cautioned that the true scope is likely wider geographically and by industry [S5][S6].

capabilities.summary: 2023: updated PowerLess backdoor delivered via ISO images (and possibly other archives) carrying an Iraq-themed lure and a custom in-memory downloader; loaders used .NET executables built as Mixed Mode Assemblies, a technique Check Point called rarely seen in the wild [S2]. Check Point noted at the time that attacks resulting from these infections had not yet been observed [S2]. 2025: spear-phishing by email and WhatsApp using fictitious assistants to technology executives or researchers; initial messages contained no links; victims were steered to fake Gmail login pages or Google Meet invitations, some hosted on Google Sites pages mimicking Meet [S5][S6]. The phishing kits were React single page applications with minified, obfuscated code and supported Google password, SMS, email-code and app-based 2FA flows, enabling real-time relay of MFA tokens [S6]. Check Point reported messages appeared AI-assisted and that the group used more than 130 unique domains, one or two per targeted individual (per press quoting a Check Point researcher) [S5][S6].

campaigns.name: PowerLess ISO campaign against Israel-linked targets
campaigns.summary: Check Point reported an improved arsenal: ISO-delivered lures in Arabic, English and Hebrew with Iraq-related academic decoys, an in-memory downloader, and the PowerLess implant loaded through Mixed Mode Assembly .NET binaries [S2].

campaigns.name: Spear-phishing of Israeli technology academics, journalists and cybersecurity experts
campaigns.summary: Email and WhatsApp approaches by impersonated assistants led to fake Gmail or Google Meet pages and a React SPA kit that harvested credentials and 2FA codes, supported by 130+ domains [S4][S5][S6].

diamond.adversary: Iran-aligned cluster; Check Point believes it works for IRGC-IO and overlaps APT42/Charming Kitten/Mint Sandstorm [S2][S5].
diamond.capability: PowerLess backdoor, ISO lures, Mixed Mode Assembly loaders (2023); AI-assisted social engineering, WhatsApp/email approach, React SPA phishing kit with 2FA relay (2025) [S2][S6].
diamond.infrastructure: More than 130 domains and numerous subdomains, one or two per targeted individual, per press quoting Check Point; fake Gmail and Google Meet pages, Google Sites lures [S5][S6].
diamond.victim: Israeli academics, journalists, cybersecurity experts and researchers [S2][S5][S6].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection against Israel-linked individuals; Check Point's 2025 report is covered by press alongside Iran-Israel tension, but that framing is the outlets', not a stated Check Point objective [S5].
diamond.technology: Consumer cloud identity (Google accounts, Gmail, Meet), WhatsApp messaging, and MFA that can be relayed in real time [S6].

gaps: I could not open the Check Point primary reports (2023 and 2025) or the Check Point blog from this environment; findings rely on search-result summaries of Check Point and secondary coverage. Verify details against research.checkpoint.com before use [S4].
Whether 2023 infections led to follow-on intrusions is not stated; Check Point said none had been observed at the time [S2].
Exact relationship to APT42, APT35/Charming Kitten and Mint Sandstorm is only characterized as overlap or alignment; Microsoft's own mapping of this cluster was not located.
Earliest activity date, malware C2 details, victim counts and any non-Israeli targeting are not available in the sources gathered.
The 130+ domain figure comes from press quoting a Check Point researcher; the figure and indicator list were not verified against the report.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is personal and institutional identity (Google accounts, WhatsApp) of researchers, academics and cyber experts who sit near government and defense work. STEP 2: The actor uses one or two disposable domains per victim and AI-polished, link-free first contact, which defeats blocklists and early filtering [S5][S6]. STEP 3: Template is rapport-building through an impersonated assistant, then a fake Gmail or Meet page that relays passwords and MFA codes [S6]; earlier template was ISO, in-memory downloader, PowerLess [S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued credential harvesting against Israel-linked experts and academics. MDCOA is extension of the same approach to allied-government or DoD-adjacent researchers and contractors, using personal accounts as a path to institutional data. Candidate indicators: unsolicited WhatsApp or email contact from unknown technology-sector assistants, newly registered per-target domains, Google Meet or Gmail lookalike pages, and ISO files arriving as lures [S2][S5][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: personal-account and messaging-app phishing against personnel and affiliated researchers sits outside most enterprise telemetry; add reporting channels for it. (2) Authorities: monitoring personal accounts is constrained; rely on awareness training, voluntary reporting and partner sharing rather than collection. (3) Mission assurance: prefer phishing-resistant MFA, since the kit relays SMS, email-code and app-based 2FA in real time [S6]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with Israeli and allied CERTs and industry partners, noting that vendor cluster boundaries (APT42, Charming Kitten, Mint Sandstorm) are not identical.

provenance.importedSummary: Educated Manticore is an Iranian APT group aligned with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, primarily engaged in espionage targeting government, military, and academic sectors. The group employs spear-phishing tactics, utilizing custom backdoors like POWERLESS and phishing kits designed as SPAs to harvest credentials. Their operations have included impersonating credible figures to lure victims and using ISO images to initiate infection chains. Educated Manticore's activities are characterized by rapid domain setup and aggressive spear-phishing campaigns, particularly against Israeli individuals.
